title: Outlook for Mac: Purview DLP policy tips (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, administrator opt-in default and documented controls are supported. It correctly reports Microsoft's conflicting Mac support documentation and limits its licensing uncertainty to Mac-specific requirements. Minor corrections concern abbreviated rule paths and a reporting checklist step without a controls-table row.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The printed Purview Custom-policy wizard path reaches User notifications > Policy tips for an Exchange email rule.
claims.quote: Select Custom from the Categories list. Select Custom from the Regulations list. ... Select Full directory under Admin units. ... Set the User notifications toggle to On. Select Policy tips
claims.fix: Include the omitted list headings in controls[1].ui and its table copy: 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom > Admin units > Full directory > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > Policy tips'. The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-osp-get-started supports this route.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <rule name> -Policy <policy name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipCustomText "<text>" creates a rule with owner notification and custom policy-tip text.
claims.quote: The NotifyUser parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that notifies the specified users ... Owner ... The NotifyPolicyTipCustomText parameter specifies the custom text in the Policy Tip notification message

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The printed Purview rule path reaches the page containing the policy-tip override choice.
claims.quote: Set the User notifications toggle to On. Select Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only). If already selected, uncheck the Allow override from M365 services option.
claims.fix: Use the complete walkthrough route to the row's deciding option in controls[2].ui and its table copy: 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom > Admin units > Full directory > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only) > Allow override from M365 services'. Keep the note identifying this as the Exchange email walkthrough, not a claim that Mac supports the oversharing dialog. The route is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-osp-get-started.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to review override justifications, but the controls table has no reporting row for that step.
claims.quote: Review override justifications in the DLP reports in the Reports section of the Microsoft Purview portal. The table covers only tip-UI availability, rule tip text and rule overrides.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist bullet 'Review override justifications in the DLP reports in the Reports section of the Microsoft Purview portal.' Its reporting fact can remain in Risk assessment; do not add a control row during this correction.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: NotifyAllowOverride requires BlockAccess true and an appropriate BlockAccessScope for an email override option to appear.
claims.quote: If you set the NotifyAllowOverride action to WithoutJustification or WithJustification or FalsePositives, make sure BlockAccess is set to true and BlockAccessScope has appropriate value. Otherwise, the policy tip comes up but the user doesn't find an option to override the email with justification.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Blocking is configured in the DLP rule rather than being an autonomous action introduced by the tip UI.
claims.quote: The BlockAccess parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks access to the source item when the conditions of the rule are met.
